title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. C is an elliptic curve over Q̄. G is its motivic Galois group (here the same as its Mumford–Tate group). If C has no CM, G = GL(2)_Q. If C has CM by an imaginary quadratic field K, G = Res_{K/Q} G_m, a 2-dimensional torus.

The period point. The de Rham–Betti comparison H^1_B(C,Q)⊗C ≅ H^1_dR(C/Q̄)⊗C, written in a Q-basis of Betti and a Q̄-basis of de Rham, gives a period matrix g in G(C). Changing the de Rham basis multiplies it by G(Q̄), hence g ∈ G(C)/G(Q̄). In modern terms g is a C-point of the period torsor P = Isom^⊗(ω_B ⊗ Q̄, ω_dR), which is a G-torsor. Concretely, in the non-CM case with de Rham basis ω = dx/y, η = x dx/y, g is the matrix (ω1 ω2; η1 η2) of periods and quasi-periods.

(a) Grothendieck's period conjecture for C: trdeg Q(g) = dim G, i.e. 4 without CM and 2 with CM. In the non-CM case the 4 includes 2πi through the Legendre relation det g = ω1η2 − ω2η1 = 2πi. This matches the previous page: the normalised periods have transcendence degree 3, plus 1 for 2πi.

(b) A weaker question. Let T be the Q̄-Zariski closure of g in G_Q̄, translated so that it contains e. Let H be the algebraic group generated by T. Does H = G? Equivalently: is the period point 'group-theoretically generic', i.e. not trapped in a coset of a proper subgroup? This is the torsor-theoretic weakening of (a), close to what later became the question of whether the Zariski closure of the period point is a subtorsor.

(c) The Hodge splitting. F^1 = H^0(C,Ω^1) = Q̄·ω is defined over Q̄. The complementary line H^{0,1} = conj(F^1) inside H^1_dR ⊗ C is spanned by η + hω, with h ∈ C/Q̄ well defined up to the choice of η. Computing with periods gives h = −(η1 ω̄2 − η2 ω̄1)/(ω1 ω̄2 − ω2 ω̄1), i.e. up to normalisation h ~ η1/ω1 − π/(ω1² Im τ). This is essentially (ω1/π)^{-2}-normalised E2*(τ), the non-holomorphic weight-2 Eisenstein series.

Question: can h be algebraic, or is it transcendental when C has no CM? The margin note records that with CM, h ∈ Q̄. That is right: the K-eigenspace decomposition of H^1_dR is defined over Q̄ and coincides with the Hodge decomposition. Classically this is the algebraicity of (ω/π)² E2*(τ) at CM points (Ramanujan, Masser).

Purpose. The page specialises to elliptic curves the conjecture of p.11: the period point is generic in G, i.e. Q̄-Zariski-dense in the torsor. It then asks about a second, non-period transcendental invariant: the position of the Hodge splitting relative to the Q̄-structure. The next page announces 'Hodge functors on the category of motives', comparing the fibre functors.
errors: G(C)/G(Q̄) as written does not give a well-defined field 'Q(g)'. One should take Q̄(g) for a representative, or the Q̄-Zariski closure of the coset; transcendence degree over Q or Q̄ is the same.

The Q̄-Zariski closure of a single point is irreducible, so 'pas nécessairement connexe' is superfluous over Q̄; it would only matter for a Q-closure. 'Contenant e' presupposes translating g by an element of G(Q̄) so that it lies in its own locus.
dim G = 4 in the non-CM case counts 2πi (det g = 2πi by Legendre). This is consistent with p.11 but should be kept in mind: without 2πi the expected degree is 3.

In (c), h algebraic versus transcendental is not purely a statement about the period field Q(g): h involves complex conjugates of periods. So (a) does not by itself imply transcendence of h except when C is defined over R.

ideas.what: Transcendence degree of the period field of an elliptic curve over Q̄ equals the dimension of its motivic Galois group (4 or 2)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck period conjecture (elliptic curve case); in the CM case Chudnovsky's theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (stated in a 1966 footnote, publicised by André/Lang); CM case proved by G. Chudnovsky (c.1976); non-CM case open, Chudnovsky trdeg ≥ 2
ideas.where_published: Footnote in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHÉS 29, 1966); the motivic-Galois-group formulation is mainly known via André

ideas.what: Question whether the algebraic group generated by the Q̄-locus of the period point is all of G
ideas.modern_name: Weak (group-generation / subtorsor) form of the period conjecture; Zariski closure of the period point in the period torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: André (motivic Galois / period torsor formulations, 1990s–2004); related known results via Wüstholz's analytic subgroup theorem and Masser/Chudnovsky

ideas.what: Transcendental parameter h measuring the Hodge splitting H^{0,1} ⊂ H^1_dR⊗C relative to the Q̄-structure; algebraic in the CM case; asks whether it is transcendental otherwise
ideas.modern_name: Algebraicity of the Hodge decomposition / values of E2*(τ) normalised by (ω/π)²; 'Hodge splitting defined over Q̄ ⇔ CM'
ideas.usually_credited_to: CM algebraicity: Ramanujan, Masser (1975), Shimura (nearly holomorphic forms at CM points), Katz (CM splitting in p-adic Eisenstein work). The non-CM converse is generally regarded as open (unsure).

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether the Q̄-algebraicity of the Hodge splitting of H^1_dR characterises CM elliptic curves, i.e. whether h is transcendental in the non-CM case. To my knowledge this is still open in general for non-CM curves over Q̄. It follows from the period conjecture applied to C × C̄ (or to C alone if C is defined over R), not from (a) for C alone. It is a clean 'Hodge-theoretic special point' question that is distinct from the Schneider / Cohen / Shiga–Wolfart characterisation of CM by algebraicity of τ.
missed.quote: Peut-on avoir h ∈ Q̄, ou h est-il transcendant sur Q [cas où C n'a pas de multiplication complexe] ... NB Si C a de la multiplication complexe, on a h ∈ Q̄ !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Algebraicity of E2*-type invariants and of Hodge splittings at special points is used in p-adic L-functions (Katz) and in Shimura-variety algebraicity theorems. A proof that 'Hodge splitting over Q̄ ⇒ CM' for elliptic curves (or abelian varieties) would be a new transcendence result. Grothendieck frames it motivically, via the motivic Galois group and comparison of fibre functors.

missed.claim: Question (b) formulates a group-theoretic weakening of the period conjecture: the algebraic group generated by the Zariski closure of the period point is the full motivic Galois group. For elliptic curves this weakening is plausibly provable unconditionally. Chudnovsky gives trdeg ≥ 2; Masser/Wüstholz give Q̄-linear independence of 1, ω_i, η_i, 2πi, so the locus is not in a hyperplane. Together these appear to exclude the proper connected subgroups of GL2. I have not seen this specific reformulation highlighted as Grothendieck's.
missed.quote: Soit T le lieu de g sur G_Q̄, variété ... contenant e, et soit H le groupe engendré par T. A-t-on H = G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates André-style subtorsor statements and the 'generic period point' viewpoint. It offers a provable intermediate between Wüstholz-type linear results and the full algebraic-independence conjecture.

deep.surprise_reason: Item (a) is the known Grothendieck period conjecture, already credited to him. Items (b) and (c) are genuinely unpublished questions in motivic language. The CM remark is classical, and the non-CM transcendence of the Hodge-splitting parameter is a natural but little-advertised question. These are interesting archival details but not a major missed result.
transcription_corrections: '[car si C n'a pas de multiplication complexe]' should read '[cas où C n'a pas de multiplication complexe]'.

'définissant l'application des réseaux transcendante de Betti dans celui de de Rham' is more plausibly 'définissant l'application transcendante de Betti dans celle de de Rham'; the word before 'transcendante' is uncertain.
Margin: 'NB Si C a de la multiplication complexe, on a h ∈ Q̄ !' is confirmed.
In (b) the struck text is 'R...' before 'variété'; the phrase 'et son engendré' (or similar) after 'par T.' is crossed out.
